basis: Compiere, Inc. raised its first outside round, $6M, from New Enterprise Associates in June 2006, with NEA partners joining the board (the company's release of 2006-06-20; Wikipedia says the same).

note: Open-source ERP vendor of Redwood City. NEA's $6M of June 2006 was the company's first outside round, above the era's $1.5M seed ceiling, so Series A. Consona bought Compiere on 2010-06-16 (Kroll transaction note; Wikipedia), terms not disclosed.

basis: Connect Ventures, the CAA and NEA partnership, led Deep Voodoo's $20M round of December 2022, its first outside capital (TechCrunch, Variety, Wikipedia). Connect Ventures I, L.P. is on NEA's Form ADV Schedule 7.B, so this is NEA fund money (decisions.md, Connect Ventures re-derivation).

note: AI visual effects studio of Trey Parker and Matt Stone, spun out of Park County, which funded it until the $20M Connect Ventures round of December 2022; an unnamed first outside round above the 2022 seed ceiling ($8M), so Series A. Momentum check 2026-09-30 (Google News): no later priced round and no $1B+ round; still operating (THR, 2026-03-31).

basis: Synopsys' S-3 of 1998-11-25 registers the Synopsys shares Everest's stockholders received when Synopsys bought Everest Design Automation in November 1998, and lists New Enterprise Associates VII (163,400 shares), NEA Presidents Fund and NEA Ventures 1998 among them: NEA funds held Everest. The firm's archived Synopsys page adds 'Acquired Everest Design for stock 10/98' (D8).

note: Private developer of shape-based physical design (routing) software for chips, bought by Synopsys for stock under a merger agreement of 1998-10-26, closed 1998-11-20 (the S-3). No source names NEA's round or dates its entry, and none places the company's city.

basis: Jomboy Media's $5M round of May 2022 'came by way of Connect Ventures, a partnership with Creative Artists Agency (CAA) and global venture capital firm New Enterprise Associates (NEA)', with Connect's Adam Friedman joining the board (Dodger Blue, 2022-05-06). Connect Ventures I is an NEA fund (Form ADV).

note: New York baseball media company (Business Journals: 'Jomboy Media of New York'). Connect's entry was an unnamed $5M round that followed the founder's 2018 raise and $1M in February 2021, so it is not the first round and no source names it; the stage stays undetermined. MLB took an undisclosed minority stake in June 2025; still operating (Fubo channel, April 2026).

basis: The firm's own archived Synopsys page (first investment 1994, Historic) reads 'Acquired Logic Modeling for stock 3/94': NEA's Synopsys stock was the consideration for its Logic Modeling position, so Logic Modeling is the member and Synopsys stays out (D8).

note: Beaverton, Oregon maker of simulation models and hardware modeling systems for chip design, bought by Synopsys for stock in March 1994 (the firm's Synopsys page; EEJournal's EDA history). NEA's entry round and year are not on record. Aligned with the Sutter Hill and Sequoia rows (acquired, US, Beaverton).

basis: Mojito's $20M first round (release of 2021-10-21, led by Future Perfect Ventures) had a strategic investment from 'Connect Ventures, an investment partnership between ... CAA and global venture capital firm New Enterprise Associates (NEA)'. Connect Ventures I is an NEA fund (Form ADV).

note: NFT commerce suite spun out of Serotonin, dateline New York. Its first round, $20M, is unnamed and above the 2021 seed ceiling ($6M), so Series A. The last dated trace of the company is the Coinbase case study of August 2023 and its president's Wikipedia page still names it; no sale or shutdown found (Google News, 2026-09-30), so private.

basis: Music AI's $40M Series A 'was led by Connect Ventures, an investment partnership between CAA and venture capital firm New Enterprise Associates (NEA)', with monashees (Music Business Worldwide, 2025-01-22; LatamList the same). Connect Ventures I is an NEA fund (Form ADV).

note: Music AI (the Moises app), Salt Lake City, founded by Brazilians. Connect Ventures entered as lead of the $40M Series A ($30M primary, $10M secondary) after monashees' $8.6M seed of 2022. Momentum check 2026-09-30 (Google News): no later round and no $1B+ priced round.

basis: The firm's own CMS carries an entry for Niroda Therapeutics (draft dated 2026-07-22, not yet published): 'developing non-opioid pain treatments', status Private, investment type Current, NEA team Scott Gottlieb, Ali Behbahani and J.C. Lopez. BB Biotech's Q2 2026 slides add Niroda as a new private position, so a 2026 private round exists. The firm's own listing, read from an unpublished draft.

note: U.S. biotech (Korea Biomedical Review) that in-licensed Daewoong affiliate iN Therapeutics' NaV1.7 non-opioid pain candidate in December 2025; Dun & Bradstreet's directory lists it in Short Hills, New Jersey. No round is announced (Google News and web search, 2026-09-30) and the firm's label is Early, which is not a round word, so the stage is undetermined.

basis: Connect Ventures, which 'originally began as an investment partnership between CAA and NEA in 2020', has made investments in 'TMRW Sports, OpenSea, Slash, and Jomboy Media' (citybiz and THR, 2026-01-26). Connect Ventures I is an NEA fund (Form ADV Schedule 7.B).

note: NFT marketplace. The Block names Creative Artists Agency among the participants in the $100M Series B of July 2021 at $1.5B; Tracxn (vendor, listed not cited) places Connect Ventures in that round, so the entry reads the Series B, Growth, at medium. Mark: the $300M Series C at $13.3B of 2022-01-04 led by Paradigm and Coatue (TechCrunch), the last priced primary; stale. City aligned with the a16z, Coatue, Tiger and YC rows (Wikipedia's lede now says Miami, undated).

basis: Connetics (Connective Therapeutics) listed in February 1996. NEA's only position is the 1,250,000 shares New Enterprise Associates VIII (a 1998 fund), NEA Presidents Fund and NEA Ventures 1998 bought in the November 1998 private placement (the S-3 of 1998-12-16 registering the 'November 1998 Investors'), and NEA's 13G of 1999-02-16 names only those vehicles. X1: a PIPE into an already listed company with no earlier NEA private round; if Erik rules a PIPE a venture entry, this row enters at Growth.

note: Gene medicine developer of The Woodlands, Texas (its EDGAR address). It merged with Megabios in March 1999 to form Valentis (DEFM14A of 1999-02-22, deregistered 1999-03-18), so acquired.

Maker of ADCON anti-adhesion gels, Cleveland, Ohio (its EDGAR address). It filed Chapter 11 on 2002-05-09 (8-K of 2002-05-10) and deregistered on 2002-05-15; no sale of the business is on record, so defunct.

Asian web hosting and data center operator headquartered in San Mateo. It sold its Korean and Taiwan operations in 2001-02 and its board authorized dissolution and wind-up on 2002-03-07 (8-K of 2002-03-08). Aligned with the IVP row.
Sports medicine device maker of Marlborough, Massachusetts. It signed a merger agreement with Johnson & Johnson on 1999-11-08 (8-K of 1999-11-19) and was absorbed as a J&J subsidiary.

basis: The same company as the inventiva-pharma row, already not_member under X1: Inventiva has been listed on Euronext Paris since February 2017, and NEA's first purchase was the capital increase of 2019-09-20, priced at the Euronext close and subscribed beside BVF and Novo (the July 2020 Nasdaq prospectus); the 13D filings behind this row come after that. If Erik rules a PIPE a venture entry, the company enters at Growth once, on one of the two slugs.

note: Maker of laser film digitizers for medical imaging, Sunnyvale. Eastman Kodak agreed to acquire it on 2000-11-09 (8-K of 2000-11-13; deregistered January 2001).

Electronic health record company of Hillsboro, Oregon. After its Chapter 11 filing of 2002-01-24, the court approved the sale of substantially all of its Digital Health Records business to GE Medical Systems Information Technologies for about $35.3M, closed 2002-03-25 (8-K/A of 2002-04-16); GE is the successor.

Antibacterial drug developer of Mountain View, renamed Essential Therapeutics after its 2001 merger with Althexis and Maret (later Waltham). It filed Chapter 11 on 2003-05-01; the plan effective 2003-10-21 cancelled the common stock and left the company with its preferred holders (8-K of 2003-10-22), and no later operation is on record. Aligned with the IVP row.

Online loyalty and rewards marketing company (ClickRewards), San Francisco. It filed Chapter 11 on 2001-10-05 and its assets were auctioned piecemeal to six high bidders in November 2001 (8-K of 2001-12-03); no buyer took the business as a whole, so defunct.

Network equipment maker of Herndon, Virginia, renamed NX Networks after its 2000 merger with OpenROUTE Networks. It filed Chapter 11 on 2001-11-01, and on 2002-03-06 the court approved the sale of its business to nsgdata.com (8-K of 2002-03-14); nsgdata.com is the successor.
Maker of the ObjectStore object database, Burlington, Massachusetts; renamed eXcelon in January 2000 and bought by Progress Software in December 2002 (DEFM14A of 2002-11-18; Wikipedia).
Broadband access equipment maker of Santa Barbara (reverse-merged into Accelerated Networks in 2002). Calix acquired it in February 2011 (DEFM14A of 2010-12-15; delisted 2011-02-22).
